title: KOFFVQA: An Objectively Evaluated Free-form VQA Benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models in the Korean Language

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model performance on a Korean-language visual question answering benchmark to measure disparities in capabilities compared to standard English benchmarks, specifically observing instances where models fail to process Korean instructions, generate incoherent Korean, or default to answering in English.

Assessing cultural knowledge representation through a dedicated 'Recognition-KO' question subcategory that tests the model's ability to recognize visual subjects specific to and well-known within Korean culture (e.g., local places, artworks, and people) as opposed to globally recognized subjects.

Measuring the subjectivity, unreliability, and self-preference bias of LLM-as-a-judge and VLM-as-a-judge methods by comparing traditional subjective scoring against objective, pre-defined fine-grained grading criteria, and analyzing how visual inputs can induce hallucination-driven bias in automated judges.
